title: Forcing orders and generic filters

based_on.title: Set Theory
based_on.pages: 97–99 (forcing orders, generic filters and Cohen forcing; revision 2026-01-31)

based_on.title: Forcing Summer School Lecture Notes
based_on.pages: 26–27 (§10.1, Definition 10.1, Lemma 10.2 and Proposition 10.5; section by Justin Palumbo; revised 2014-09-06)

summary: Construct generic filters through countably many dense requirements and obtain a binary sequence different from every sequence in the ground model.
abstract: A finite binary partial function specifies only finitely many bits of an infinite sequence. Extending these partial functions can meet any countable list of dense requirements, where each requirement can be reached by strengthening any current approximation. If a countable transitive model of ZFC is given, this construction produces a filter meeting every dense set belonging to that model. Its compatible finite approximations combine into a total binary sequence, and suitable dense requirements make the sequence differ from every binary sequence in the original model. Directedness of the filter, absoluteness of density, and the distinction between internal and external countability explain why the construction works.
